name: Ancient Capitals of Asuka and Fujiwara
description: In the southern Nara Basin, Asuka and Fujiwara were Japan's first true capitals, home to the court from 588 to 710. Nineteen scattered sites survive, including palace foundations, temples and grassy burial mounds. Among them is Asuka-dera, the country's first Buddhist temple. Walking here, you trace the roots of Japanese government, which later shaped Nara and Kyoto.
